# Recreation Prompt

Recreate **Pressure Cook County**, a mobile portrait free-roam action sandbox preserving a wanted-heat chase game. The player is a desperate suburban chemistry operator represented by a yellow hazmat/apron silhouette. They move with a bottom-left joystick, rotate/zoom the camera, switch between alibi hands and a side scheme, attack, summon or enter laundering vans, and survive escalating HEAT. Buildings are suburban tract homes, laundromats, strip-mall labs, and cartel safehouses. Player-caused takedowns raise HEAT up to five stars; pursuer vehicles spawn and chase; health is NERVE; zero NERVE produces a BUSTED/moral-collapse restart screen. Use procedural Canvas art, toxic amber/green palette, desert-suburb dread, satire, dark irony, and touch-friendly portrait HUD/controls.

Source-truth guardrail: preserve input meanings, heat escalation/decay, collision blockers, vehicle interaction, pursuit pressure, health failure, and restart semantics.
blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint

## Current Game Identity
- genre: mobile-first free-roam wanted-heat action sandbox
- objective: survive in an open map while moving, attacking, switching weapons, using vehicles, and managing escalating heat
- input model: virtual joystick plus touch buttons for attack, interact/summon/enter/exit, weapon switch, camera rotate, and zoom
- core loop: roam the map, collide with blockers, interact with cars, attack NPCs/cars, trigger wanted heat, evade pursuers, and survive health damage
- fail/friction state: health reaches zero after pursuit/contact/combat pressure; play stops and restart is offered

## Protected Mechanics
- Joystick movement relative to camera orientation, camera rotate, and zoom remain protected.
- Vehicle summon/enter/exit and vehicle driving remain protected.
- Attack and weapon switch remain protected with fist/sidearm semantics.
- Wanted heat escalates to five stars after player-caused takedowns and decays over time.
- Pursuer vehicles spawn under heat and chase the player; collision blockers constrain movement.
- No win state was introduced; consequence/failure semantics remain health-to-zero restart.

## Safe Theming Surfaces
HUD terms, entity silhouettes, city/building art, background ambience, particle feedback, start/death copy, palette, typography, sound labels, and mobile chrome are safe to transform because they do not change rule truth.
